details: The U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) for October came in higher than anticipated, with headline inflation rising 0.4% month-over-month and core CPI increasing 0.3%. This unexpected rise in inflation has fueled concerns that the Federal Reserve may consider further interest rate hikes, with some officials, like Fed Governor Christopher Waller, indicating a potential 50-basis-point increase if price pressures persist. The news triggered a sharp downturn across the cryptocurrency market, pushing Bitcoin below the $73,000 mark and leading to over $170 million in liquidations of leveraged long positions. Concurrently, US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded their third consecutive day of net outflows, totaling $201 million, which further added to the selling pressure on digital assets. Ethereum and other altcoins also experienced significant price declines.
title: US Inflation Exceeds Expectations, Triggers Crypto Sell-Off & ETF Outflows

details: The Bank of Russia has announced that regulated exchanges will be permitted to offer organized trading of cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Tether's USDT, starting November 22. This initiative is contingent on the central bank's approval of the exchanges' trading rules and precedes the Moscow Exchange's planned Bitcoin launch on December 1. Under the new regulations, non-qualified investors will have an annual purchase limit of 300,000 rubles (approximately $3,600), while qualified investors will face no such cap. Both categories of investors will be required to pass a knowledge test and acknowledge risk disclosures before trading.
title: Russia to Permit Organized Cryptocurrency Trading from November 22
